purpose: Apply the broad program's formal-versus-lived recovery ladder to named public remedy episodes without inferring recipient outcomes from institutional announcements.
status_vocabulary: observed means the cited record directly supports the stage; reported means an institution reports it but recipient-level confirmation is absent; partial means some practical use is observed but the full outcome is not; open means not observed; failed means later evidence contradicts durability.

cases.formal_status: observed: reinstatement, continuity, Rohingya translation, and $18,035.56 lost-pay order
cases.received: open: post-order payment and actual reinstatement are not observed
cases.usable: open: later work access and communication change are not observed
cases.adequate: open: lost-pay adequacy and household security are not observed
cases.durable: open: return, recurrence, and later livelihood are not observed
cases.trusted: open: trust, bargaining, and exit are not observed
cases.boundary: The decision establishes a culturally and materially consequential remedy order, not completed recovery.

cases.formal_status: observed: voluntary reactivation followed by a formal reactivation order
cases.received: partial: post-reactivation work and ordinary payment are observed; lost-remuneration receipt is not
cases.adequate: open: net recovery and lost-remuneration adequacy are not observed
cases.durable: open: more than 150 trips are observed, but later access and non-retaliation are not
cases.trusted: open: alternatives, trust, and practical exit are not observed
cases.boundary: Operational use after restoration is stronger than a paper order but does not prove complete recovery.

cases.formal_status: observed: correct-rate change and $27,424.88 gross compensation order
cases.received: partial: $4,000 payment is documented, while historical wages remained unpaid and full-order receipt is not verified
cases.usable: partial: new employment is observed; quality and freedom of the alternative are not observed
cases.adequate: open: residual loss and financial recovery are not observed
cases.durable: open: later job duration and repeat underpayment are not observed
cases.trusted: partial: refusal to return is linked to broken trust and emotional stress; trust recovery is not observed
cases.boundary: The case closes forced exit and partial payment more strongly than it closes recovery.

cases.formal_status: observed: settlement, recruitment controls, monitoring, and completed fund processing are reported
cases.received: reported: the agency reports fund exhaustion, but individual receipt, amount, date, and worker confirmation are not published
cases.usable: open: restored consideration or hiring is not observed
cases.adequate: open: individual compensation adequacy and lost opportunity are not observed
cases.durable: open: monitoring findings and recurrence are not observed
cases.trusted: open: applicant trust, later application, and exit are not observed
cases.boundary: A completed aggregate fund is not an applicant-level receipt or restored-opportunity measure.

cases.received: reported: 3,759 recipients cashed a previous check; the third check is not yet verified
cases.usable: open: account correction and ability to use the funds are not observed
cases.adequate: open: residual account harm and business recovery are not observed
cases.durable: open: business survival, employment, and repeat harm are not observed
cases.trusted: open: continued use, switching, and trust are not observed
cases.boundary: A prior cashed check supports a reported receipt stage for that distribution, not the third payment or durable recovery.

cases.formal_status: observed: IER intervention and employer correction
cases.received: reported: official account says the worker was paid approximately $420 in back pay; independent receipt and payment date are not retained
cases.usable: reported: worker reportedly returned to work the following day
cases.adequate: open: wage adequacy, household effect, and residual loss are not observed
cases.durable: open: later employment, recurrence, and durable protection are not observed
cases.trusted: open: worker-reported fairness, trust, bargaining, switching, and exit are not observed
cases.boundary: This is a positive implementation counterexample: reported rapid restoration and payment exist, while independently verified and durable recovery remain unmeasured.

cases.formal_status: observed: $100 million court-entered judgment, $79 million driver allocation, $10 million FTC driver-distribution allocation, and 10-year earnings verification
cases.received: partial/reported: payments began in mid-2025 and some drivers should have payment-date emails; individual receipt, amount, and unresolved count are not published
cases.usable: open: corrected pay records, restored earnings opportunity, and schedule control are not observed
cases.adequate: open: driver-level amount owed, amount received, and residual loss are not observed
cases.durable: open: 10-year compliance is ordered, but actual compliance, recurrence, continued work, and alternatives are not observed
cases.trusted: open: trust, switching, organizing, and exit are not observed
cases.boundary: This is stronger than an allocation-only settlement because payment timing and partial processing status are visible, but it remains far from same-driver recovery.

cases.formal_status: observed: court-entered judgment, $24.8 million FTC payment, $200,000 Illinois contribution, and prospective driver/diner/restaurant controls
cases.received: reported: more than $23.8 million sent in 640,038 payments; individual cashing or PayPal acceptance is not verified
cases.usable: open: account correction, restored driver income, diner access, or restaurant listing visibility are not observed
cases.adequate: open: group-specific loss, payment amount, and adequacy are not observed
cases.durable: open: control use, enforcement, repeat exposure, sales/earnings, and continued platform use are not observed
cases.trusted: open: fairness, trust, switching, collective action, and exit are not observed
cases.boundary: The route adds a multi-sided remedy and aggregate distribution stage, but group-specific lived recovery remains unlinked.

cases.formal_status: observed: $61,710,583 compensation obligation, distribution rounds, and Zelle reissue route
cases.received: reported: more than $60.6 million distributed, 2,806 successful Zelle reissue payments, and 130,952 drivers reported fully compensated; driver-level receipt is not retained
cases.usable: open: individual payment usability, fees, timing, and remaining loss are not observed
cases.adequate: open: amount due versus amount received and household recovery are not observed
cases.durable: open: continued work, alternative work, and later income security are not observed
cases.trusted: open: worker-reported fairness, bargaining, trust, and exit are not observed
cases.boundary: Aggregate payment use is stronger than a reserved fund but is not same-driver receipt, adequacy, or later recovery.

cases.formal_status: observed: recall and free-repair offers, followed by a repeat-remedy route
cases.received: open: owner-level repair completion is not observed
cases.usable: failed: the later recall reports the earlier repair was ineffective
cases.adequate: failed/open: the first repair did not resolve the safety issue; second-repair adequacy is not observed
cases.durable: failed: later remedy expansion documents failed durability of the initial repair
cases.trusted: open: safe continued use, replacement, switching, and trust are not observed
cases.boundary: This is a direct counterexample to treating remedy offer or implementation as durable protection.

cases.formal_status: reported: $18,000 compensation order followed by court enforcement and a further balance order
cases.received: partial/reported: $7,000 was reported paid, while $5,008 remained outstanding after tax at the enforcement stage
cases.usable: open: the record does not show whether the money received restored usable income or whether employment access was restored
cases.adequate: failed/open: a material balance remained outstanding; household adequacy and final payment are not observed
cases.durable: open: later work, recurrence, and continued livelihood security are not observed
cases.trusted: open: worker-reported trust, meaning, switching, and exit are not observed
cases.boundary: Partial payment and enforcement are stronger than an order-only record, but they do not establish final receipt, restored employment, adequate recovery, or durable security.

cases.formal_status: observed: union-supported return, three months back pay, prior-service recognition, and later dismissal decision
cases.received: reported: back pay and service recognition were part of the return agreement; independent payment confirmation is not retained
cases.usable: observed/partial: the worker returned and worked for a period, but later workplace conditions and safety conflict are not fully observed
cases.adequate: open: health, household, income, leave, and benefit adequacy are not measured
cases.durable: failed/open: the observed employment relationship ended in a later dismissal; post-dismissal livelihood and recovery are unknown
cases.trusted: open: the decision records a dispute over trust expectations but no standardized worker trust or later meaning measure
cases.boundary: This is a rare later-work follow-up: interim restoration is observed, followed by a later employment rupture. It does not establish why the rupture occurred or what happened afterward.

cases.formal_status: observed: unfair-dismissal finding, reinstatement/continuity order, back-pay implementation, and Full Bench correction
cases.received: observed/reported: back pay was paid and continuity was maintained, but actual work access was not restored
cases.usable: failed/open: the worker was not permitted to return while a risk assessment proceeded; later usable role access is not observed
cases.adequate: open: net payment, benefits, health, household security, and alternative compensation are not measured
cases.durable: failed/open: the observed remedy did not produce actual return during the recorded period; later work and recovery are unknown
cases.trusted: open: no worker-reported trust, dignity, or later institutional meaning measure is retained
cases.boundary: This is a strong money-versus-access counterexample: payment and continuity were implemented while actual return was withheld. It does not establish the final remedy or later livelihood.

portfolio_reading.interpretation: Across these deliberately selected named routes, institutional action is consistently more visible than verified recipient receipt, adequacy, durability, or trust. Three selected routes document a later failure or rupture of the initially observed remedy or protection, but this is a coverage finding, not a failure rate.

next_action: Use these fields when touching additional retained ledgers; prioritize same-unit recipient confirmation, amount/timing, practical use, repeat-harm checks, and later trust or exit before adding another generic response count.
